content:
The test image shows a corn stalk split open, revealing shredded internal tissue with stringy vascular strands and what appears to be tiny dark specks. This is a **stem** disease.

Top candidates from the stem list: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot, Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.

The shredded pith with stringy vascular strands and dark specks strongly suggests Charcoal Stalk Rot. Let me verify with reference images, one class at a time.
Charcoal Stalk Rot reference shows shredded pith with dark areas, similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates.
Diplodia shows a broken stalk at the node but without the shredded stringy vascular strands seen in the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Anthracnose shows shiny black lesions on the exterior rind and pinkish/reddish discoloration, different from the test image. Let me check more.
Physoderma Stalk Rot shows dark spots on a green stalk, very different from the test image. Let me check more candidates.
Bacterial Stalk Rot shows external stalk with browning leaves, not the shredded internal pith seen in the test image. Let me check Purple Leaf Sheath and Common Smut stems.
Purple Leaf Sheath shows lesions on green stalks, completely different. Let me check Common Smut stem.
Common Smut shows large galls, completely different. Now let me view a second Charcoal Stalk Rot reference to confirm the match.

This is a very strong match. The second Charcoal Stalk Rot reference shows the same pattern as the test image: shredded stalk with only stringy vascular strands remaining, rotted pith, and a grey/charred appearance from tiny dark sclerotia on the vascular bundles. The test image matches this almost exactly.

All 8 reference views used across 8 different classes: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (x2), Diplodia_Stalk_Rot, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Physoderma_Stalk_Rot, Bacterial_Stalk_Rot, Purple_Leaf_Sheath, Common_Smut.

The test image clearly shows:
- Shredded internal stalk tissue with only stringy vascular strands remaining
- Rotted/destroyed pith
- Grey to dark coloring on the vascular strands (charred appearance from tiny sclerotia)

This is the hallmark of Charcoal Stalk Rot, and the second reference image (Corn_Disease_18.jpg) is nearly identical to the test image.
